_comment: Nightly mutation testing. The quality gate proves the suite passes; this
proves the suite would FAIL if the code were wrong -- the two are not the
same and coverage alone cannot tell them apart. Scope is deliberately the
three domains where a silent behaviour change costs the most: routing (which
song gets played), community (what other members see), playback (queue
integrity). Widening it is a cost decision, not a correctness one.
break=70 fails the run below a 70% mutation score. Do not raise it to the
coverage floor: a mutant that survives because the equivalent code path is
unreachable is not the same as a missing test, and chasing the last points
buys assertions on internals rather than behaviour.
_mutate_comment: No exclusion globs here on purpose. Tests live in the top-level __tests__/
directory, not beside the code, so nothing under domain/ needs excluding and
a `!domain/**/*.test.js` pattern would only add a warning that never fires.
`!**/index.js` stays: a barrel file is re-exports, and mutating it tests the
_sandbox_comment: inPlace runs mutants against the working tree instead of a copied sandbox.
The alternative was to have Stryker copy (or symlink) ../client in, because
seven assertions in __tests__/ read client source as text -- ProfilePanel,
An in-place run keeps those relative paths resolving with nothing to sync, at
the cost of mutating files under our feet: it must never run concurrently with
another gate, and a killed run can leave a mutated file behind. Recover with
`git checkout -- domain/`; the scope below is domain/ only for that reason.
